Files removed outside the app shown as missing, never as deleted; mass disappearance suspends the root
milestones.notes: Split in two on one branch (m06-import-and-reconciliation) and one PR. `npm run test:e2e` 15 passed (6 M05 + 9 new in tests/e2e/test_setup_import_ui.py: setup offer and who sees it, start empty, folder import with plan/report/finish, zip import with slip/symlink/bomb, dropped folder in setup and as folder upload, upload-folder button merge and keep-both, interrupted import resumed by selecting the folder again, missing/greyed-out/name-collision/suspended-scan states, administrator has no route into a personal setup, phone viewport). milestones.title: Optional backups
milestones.recommended_claude_code_model: Sonnet 5.5; Opus 5.5 review of key handling, pruning floor and restore authorization
milestones.objective: Optional admin-configured backup of the whole library to a separate mounted volume: periodic full backups, changed-only backups in between, compressed and encrypted by default, with a size limit that prunes the oldest whole chains (ADR-015).
acceptance_criteria: Off by default; the app works fully with no backup volume; the backup mount is validated and a same-device volume is warned about
Interval, full-every-N, size limit and minimum chains kept (default 2, warning at 1) are audited admin settings
Full runs contain everything; changed-only runs contain only added or changed files and record deletions and missing files; a chain restores by hand with tar
Archives are per root, written to a temporary name, verified and renamed; a failed run leaves no partial archive
The size limit prunes whole oldest chains only, after a verified new run; the minimum chains are never pruned and a run that cannot fit without breaking that floor does not start and warns
Suspended or inactive roots are never backed up or counted toward retention; unsupported entries, symlinks and staging files are skipped
Archives are encrypted by default with a one-time key; no content, paths or keys in logs or audit
Restores never overwrite; the web admin role cannot restore or read a personal root from a backup; owners restore their own folder
milestones.notes: Implemented 2026-10-31 (Sonnet 5.5) on branch m06-import-and-reconciliation; see docs/milestones/M06c-design-and-plan.md (acceptance table with test names, layout, manual restore procedure, deviations and open questions). Evidence: `npm run check` clean; `npm run check:web` tsc strict + 17 vitest tests; `npm run check:api` ruff/format/mypy strict clean, 389 passed / 1 skipped (new tests/unit/api/test_backup.py, 58 tests on real files and a real tar: settings and volume validation, off by default, full and changed-only runs, add/change/rename/delete/missing chains restored with the host tar and rm, per-root archives, unsupported entries/symlinks/FIFOs/hardlinks/staging files/undecodable names skipped, suspended and inactive roots skipped and never pruned, changing files retried and deferred, failed and interrupted runs leave nothing, pruning of whole oldest chains after a verified run, minimum-chains floor, refusal when a run cannot fit, estimate from the last compression ratio, scheduler due logic, encryption (ciphertext has no names or content, wrong/truncated/damaged archives fail cleanly, key shown once and nowhere stored), rotation and key loss, CLI verify/list/decrypt, restore into a new folder without overwriting, restore authorization (owner only for a personal root, administrator for the shared tree, uniform 403, no administrator bypass), unsafe archive members, no content/paths/keys in logs or audit); `npm run test:compose` 26 passed (3 new in tests/integration/compose/test_backup_stack.py on PostgreSQL behind nginx with docker-compose.backup.yml: migration 0008, enable and run through the API, encrypted archive on the bind-mounted volume verified by the CLI in the container, restore into a new folder, member refused, restart keeps the settings, nested backup path refused at startup, no mount without the override); `npm run test:e2e` 19 passed (2 new in tests/e2e/test_ui_backups.py). Code: apps/api/app/backup/{crypto,store,volume,engine,retention,restore,service,cli}.py, api/backups.py, migration 0008_backups, config.py backup_* settings, main.py wiring, requirements.txt (cryptography 50.0.2 now a runtime dependency: add to the pre-release license audit), deploy/docker-compose.backup.yml, apps/web/src/{Backups.tsx,backupForm.ts,api.ts,route.ts,App.tsx,styles.css}. Deviations and open questions for the owner (details in the design note): (1) encryption is public-key (X25519/AES-GCM), the instance holds only the public key, so a restore needs the recovery key in the request and an owner needs the key holder to hand it over; per-owner keys would need a new ADR; (2) change detection uses live lstat fingerprints against a snapshot in the application database instead of previous manifests (archives are encrypted); (3) no 'less history than intended' warning (no such setting), the page shows the full backups and days the limit holds; (4) per-root metadata dump names the owner and grantees (encrypted by default); (5) restore is whole-root into a new folder, synchronous; (6) large files that change during the read are flagged changed_during_backup and recaptured by the next run, no filesystem snapshot. Security review done 2026-10-31 and its findings fixed (see the 'Security review fixes' section of the design note; test_backup.py now 80 tests; check:api 411 passed, test:compose 26, test:e2e 19, web 17); per-root keys proposed as ADR-016 (not decided), purge of frozen-root backups and async restore left as documented follow-ups. Not verified: Linux CI run, a real second disk, a network share as backup volume, restore of a very large tree (Linux CI run now done, see below). CI: GitHub Actions (Linux) green on PR #7 (check, compose app, compose core, e2e) at 1aac642; two test timing races found by CI were fixed. Owner sign-off 2026-10-31: M06 (a, b, c) done and signed off; ADR-016 (per-root backup keys) remains Proposed; unbuilt follow-ups in 11_OPEN_DECISIONS.md items 15-17 stay open.

milestones.title: Reverse proxy and HTTPS support
milestones.recommended_claude_code_model: Sonnet 5.5; Opus 5.5 review of trusted-proxy handling
milestones.objective: Make running behind a TLS reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager first, then Caddy, nginx, Traefik, Cloudflare Tunnel) correct, documented and tested. See ADR-018.
acceptance_criteria: Client IP for throttling and audit is the real client behind an outer proxy; a spoofed X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted peer is ignored
Sign-in, CSRF/Origin check and cookies work over HTTPS through each example proxy, including a proxy that does not preserve Host (via FILECANOPY_PUBLIC_URL / ALLOWED_ORIGINS)
A large streamed upload and a download pass through each example proxy, with documented size and timeout settings and the Cloudflare body limit stated
Tested examples in deploy/proxy/ (Nginx Proxy Manager first, then Caddy, nginx, Traefik, Cloudflare Tunnel) and README remote-access section updated; optional HSTS
required_tests: compose test with an outer proxy container: real client IP, throttle isolation per client

milestones.title: Per-root backup keys and owner recovery (ADR-016)
milestones.recommended_claude_code_model: Sonnet 5.5 implementation; independent security review before completion
milestones.objective: Implement accepted ADR-016: separate recovery keys per storage root, owner-controlled personal recovery, optional visible administrator escrow and safe legacy archive migration.
acceptance_criteria: Each storage root has an independent key pair; an owner's key cannot decrypt another root's archives
Personal recovery key shown once to the authenticated owner with save/verification guidance; no plaintext private key persisted or logged
Personal administrator escrow off by default, enabled only by explicit owner consent, visible and audited; administrator-assisted recovery grants no silent personal-folder app access
Shared-root recovery remains administrator-controlled; losing an owner key without escrow is clearly explained as loss of access to encrypted backups
Per-root creation and rotation are serialized and cannot affect another root; old keys still decrypt their old chains
Legacy instance-key archives remain readable and clearly labelled; migration never silently deletes, rewrites or misrepresents their key scope
Restore enforces owner authorization, most restrictive backup/current privacy label and fresh Confidential reauthentication, without overwriting live files
Web and CLI recovery, escrow, rotation and upgrade paths are documented and tested with synthetic data; independent security review and all evidence recorded
required_tests: cross-root key isolation and wrong-key rejection
one-time key display, key-save verification and lost-key UX
escrow default-off, explicit consent, visibility and recovery authorization
concurrent key creation/rotation and interrupted-operation recovery
legacy/new archive coexistence, upgrade and CLI restore
Private/Confidential label preservation and idle-lock refusal
no keys or plaintext contents in logs, audit or persisted state
real PostgreSQL Compose recovery drill and browser backup/recovery flows
milestones.notes: Added at the owner's request 2026-11-03, planning only. Not started; no implementation, schema migration or milestone test execution. Scope and acceptance plan: docs/milestones/M25-design-and-plan.md. ADR-016 stays accepted and unimplemented until this work is built and verified. Dependencies are already done. M25 does not depend on M24: it may run before M24 closes if owner self-restore is included in the first beta. Numbering does not authorize publication or decide beta scope; any release advertising owner self-restore must satisfy ADR-016 first. M24 release preparation remains in progress; M25 implementation requires a separate request.
